subject: Mathematics
source: Phase F · FEAT-PF1 — author-original scaffold rows for the highest-volume AQA Y10 maths spec points. Each row provides sentence frames, a word bank, a step ladder and common pitfalls drawn from teaching practice on AQA 8300.

sentenceFrames: First, I will expand the bracket by multiplying ______ by each term inside.
Then, I will collect the like terms ______ together.

wordBank.definition: multiply each term inside the bracket by the term outside
terms with exactly the same letters and powers
make the expression as short as possible by collecting like terms
the number in front of a letter, e.g. 3 in 3x

stepLadder: Multiply each term inside the first bracket by the number outside.
Multiply each term inside the second bracket by its number, watching the sign carefully.
Write all the terms in one row.
Group like terms together (x with x, numbers with numbers).
Add or subtract the like terms to write the final answer.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting to multiply the second term in the bracket (only multiplying the first).
Sign error when expanding a bracket with a minus in front (e.g. -2(x − 4) often becomes -2x − 8 instead of -2x + 8).
rows.visualAidHint: A grid (area model) showing each multiplication helps pupils who lose track of which terms have been multiplied.

sentenceFrames: The sale price represents ______ % of the original price.
So 1% of the original price is ______ ÷ ______.

wordBank.definition: finding the original amount when you know the new amount and the percentage change
a decimal that does the percentage change in one step (e.g. 0.65 for −35%)

stepLadder: Decide what 100% represents (always the original amount).
Work out what percentage of the original you have been given.
Multiply 1% by 100 to get the original amount.
Check: apply the percentage change to your answer and see if you get back to the given price.
commonPitfalls: Treating the sale price as 100% — this gives the wrong answer.
Adding the percentage change instead of subtracting it (or vice versa).
rows.visualAidHint: A bar model showing 100% across the top and 65% across the bottom helps pupils see the proportion.

sentenceFrames: I have a right-angled triangle with sides ______, ______ and the hypotenuse ______.
I will use Pythagoras' theorem: a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.

wordBank.definition: the longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle
a² + b² = c² for the sides of a right-angled triangle

stepLadder: Identify the right angle and label the sides a, b, c (with c as the hypotenuse).
Decide whether you are finding the hypotenuse or one of the shorter sides.
Write Pythagoras' theorem in the right form (c² = a² + b² for hypotenuse, a² = c² − b² for shorter side).
Substitute the known values and calculate.
Take the square root to get the answer in cm.
commonPitfalls: Mixing up which side is the hypotenuse (it must be opposite the right angle).
Forgetting the square root at the end.
Using the wrong rearrangement when finding a shorter side (subtracting instead of adding).
rows.visualAidHint: Always sketch the triangle and label the right angle and the hypotenuse before calculating.
